sections.text: O illustrious son of Kunti! Through whatever wombs men are born, it is the Spirit Itself that conceives, and I am their Father.
Purity, Passion and Ignorance are the Qualities which the Law of nature bringeth forth. They fetter the free Spirit in all beings.
O Sinless One! Of these, Purity, being luminous, strong and invulnerable, binds one by its yearning for happiness and illumination.

We have completed chapter 13 and started discussing chapter 14. So in the last chapter we have very exhaustively discussed the relationship of the nature and the knower of the Nature, the Prakriti and Purusha, the field and its knower, that we have seen that both are Anadi, both are beginningless. But all these activities take place in Prakriti.
The self remains inactive, it becomes a witness, but its very presence makes it possible. All the activities, this field and its Knower, when come together, then only a creation comes into place. If there is a field but there is no knower, or the knower but there is no field, both cannot exist because field of the Knower only exists because there is a field and the field only exists because the Knower is there.
So this superimposition of the field on its knower creates this world of plurality as we know it. But it never really explained to us why this plurality -- in other words, why this variety. We know that the Prakriti is beginningless.
We know the Purusha is beginningless. There is no difference in Prakriti here or Prakriti there, no difference between over here and over there. Then what is it that causes all this world of plurality, the variations and modifications that we see -- that I am different from you, and you are different from the next person? This chapter deals with that aspect. Prakriti is all-pervading and everywhere, and so is the Knower.
But it is the qualities of this Prakriti that create this variety, as we know. So this chapter, the Yoga of Gunas, now talks about the nature of Prakriti. We have seen that there is no activity taking place in the Knower, the self.
All the activities, all the Karmas, are the cause and the effect of Prakriti. The very nature of things and beings creates this activity and this variety. So that will be discussed in this chapter.
The chapter opens with Lord Krishnas declaration one more time. As he has done many times before, he says parambhuyaha pravakshami Gnananam Gnanamuttamam -- Im going to tell you, I shall again declare to you the supreme knowledge, Gnananam Gnanamuttam, the best among all knowledge. What it really means is that we need to constantly keep repeating what is important, what is real and what is unreal.
In the last chapter, in a very broad brush, we have seen that how we can disassociate ourselves as the knower from the field that included my body, mind and intellect. That was the paradigm shift for us, that this body, mind and intellect is part of the field. One who knows this body, mind and intellect is the knower of this field.
That knower is the self. That self is pervading equally among all the beings. However, it never explained -- if thats the case, if the knower is the same, pervading everywhere -- why there is a variety, why I am who I am and you are who you are.
So this chapter says, if I know why I am who I am right now, if I have a guide to analyze my own self, I can introspect and say: what makes me who I am? At times Im a nice person, at times Im a very angry man. And at times Im not so nice. What makes me nice or not so nice at various times? If I can have a guide to use as a path to introspect myself, maybe I will have a better chance to understand myself as I exist as the jiva, as the individual ego -- and then can transcend that individual ego to identify with the self which is all-pervading in all of us.
Therefore, this knowledge is the most important knowledge among all the knowledges, because it allows you to introspect your own self. Yat gnatva munayha sarve param siddham ita gataha. Anytime you have to sell something to somebody, you have to make sure that there is proof.
You cant say that nobody has ever heard this before -- you are the first guinea pig Im going to try this out on, and lets see if it works. This knowledge was used by many munis. Yat gnatva -- knowing this knowledge, they attain the param siddhim, the highest supreme achievement.
The phrase after going from here is sometimes complex and can be misleading. If you dont read between the lines, the first phrase is ita gathaha -- after going from here. So we might come to the conclusion that this knowledge will be only beneficial after I die, that while Im here, it may not be possible for me to gain that knowledge.
Then yad ginatva munay ha -- all the Munis who, knowing this, have achieved the supreme state. And we all know that we started out by asking, what is the supreme state? We are looking for the supreme state where there is no limitation. For me, I am right now suffering from my limitations.
I want to get out of these limitations so that I can have eternal bliss. So am I qualified for this? And this verse can be misguiding when it says munihi sarve -- so we think this knowledge is only for the Munis. Our picture of a Muni is, a guy who is in his 70s and 80s, somewhere in the Himalayas with a white beard, surviving on just whatever he can gather.
Nothing to do with the world. But to us that a Muni is one who is contemplating within his mind. One who is contemplating about the self in his own mind is a Muni.
One who is a seeker of this knowledge is a Muni. As this knowledge becomes more and more clear to him -- yad gatva -- as this knowledge becomes clearer to him, he gets closer and closer to his goal. Once this knowledge becomes his own, he achieves that final state where there are no limitations.
Itaha kathaha -- after having gone from here. Gone from here means from this state of my understanding that this is me, that this body, mind and intellect is me, and the workings of my body and mind are my doings, and I am the enjoyer and sufferer. Once that understanding has changed -- that body, mind and intellect are part of the field, and I am just the observer who makes this body, mind, and intellect function. So Itah kath -- going from this stage of identifying with the conditioned individualized ego, which we have seen in the field and its knower.
The knower which identifies with the field becomes the individualized ego. The knower which identifies with my body, my mind, my intellect becomes me, the jiva. Once that identification is detached and I see myself as every other self, I become free from that.
Itha gath -- the Munis have come to understand this. The next verse says Idam gnanam upashitya mama sa Dharmyam Agathah. So we have two entities right now in our understanding.
One is me, who is eternally suffering -- because anytime I think I have achieved what I want, something else comes along that is higher than that. Something gets out of my control. I think I have control of all the situations, then suddenly something gets out of control.
We figure out everything is going right. And suddenly we hear that our son is not doing well. Somehow I make sure that side is taken care of.
Then we figure out the economy has shifted. We try to manage things within our control, but constantly something is getting out of our control. Then we know that there is someone who has control over everything, one who never has to worry about anything.
He doesnt have to compete for jobs with anybody. He is the Lord of all these beings. This creates a complete division -- I and him are separate.
But my goal is to constantly become him, because my goal is to become without any limitations, without any sorrows. So Im constantly trying to go from what I am to what he is. And Bhagavan says, Idam Gnanam Upashatya -- one who has taken refuge in this knowledge.
The knowledge which he has not given us yet, but hes going to give it to us. He has given us a broad brush understanding of how things work. But how to get from here to there, we dont know yet.
But he says, idam Gnanam Upasatya mama sa Dharma Agathah. One who has taken refuge in the knowledge, they become one with me. Their dharmas have become what my dharmas are.
My dharmas are limited. Right now his dharmas are unlimited. From this limitedness to unlimitedness, Bhagavan said, those munis who have understood this knowledge and became one with that knowledge have become one with me.
Sadharamyam Agatha API na upa jayante Pralayena Vihanticha. This is a broad statement for somebody like us who is worried about the next paycheck. It says that they do not take birth even at the time of creation.
We are saying, look, forget about the creation and Pralaya -- I am worried about whats happening tomorrow. But he says, theres such a person Sargiya Pina upa Jayante Pralay na Vyatanti character. And he doesnt get destroyed at the time of Pralaya.
Because we are also pretty long term planners. So we say, okay, I mean I do all of that. But then again Ill take a birth and Ill go back to the same thing all over again.
Ill realize that Im that unlimited being. But then Ill take a birth again and then Ill start from scratch all over again. Bhagavan said, no -- once you have realized who you are, there is no birth or death for you.
Then you might ask, if everybody realizes this, obviously there is no creation and there is no Pralaya, so why are we going through all of this? He says, this is self-knowledge. This is for you to get out of the misery which you are going through. You are not worried about what the others are doing.
We are not taking over his job of creating and destroying. I am only concerned about me. If the job market is bad and we have 10 of our friends who are out of a job, including yourself, who are you most worried about getting a job for? Yourself, right? Good luck to all of you, but once I get a job, Im alright.
Others may be doing whatever they are doing. Bhagavan may have whatever goal he has in this cycle of creation and dissolution. I need to get out of this misery.
The one who has understood this will never have to take birth again or die again. This in a logical, philosophical manner. He says the world keeps on going the way it is, but I understand that this Prakriti is an illusion.
The creation is a trick of my mind. If there is a lump of clay or Play-Doh, I make the shape myself and assign value to it -- that it is a doll, or its an elephant, or whatever it is. Nothing has changed in the clay itself.
But my mind has now assigned a value that its a creation created by me and I have given a name and form to it. Now if I dont assign the name and form to it and keep seeing the clay as it is, there is no creation taking place. Now when I take that clay elephant I made and destroy it back into a lump of clay, that elephant is destroyed.
If I had taken credit for that creation and assigned a name and form to it, then yes, something was destroyed. But if I never assigned a name and form to it, it has remained what it was before -- a lump of clay. Prakriti remaining Prakriti, and Purusha remaining Purusha.

These verses introduce the three gunas, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, as the fundamental qualities that bind the imperishable Self to the perishable body. Krishna states clearly: nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinam avyayam, these gunas fetter the free Spirit in all beings. Yet here is the subtle trap revealed in verse 6: even Sattva, the most luminous and pure quality, creates bondage through sukhasangena (attachment to happiness) and jnanasangena (attachment to knowledge). Notice today how your pursuit of clarity, health, and understanding, all sattvic qualities, can themselves become chains. Do you cling to your good states? Do you feel superior when you are clear-headed and peaceful?
The teaching reveals that you are the Divine Fathers seed planted in Natures womb, aham bijapradah pita. Every being, regardless of their apparent form or station, shares this sacred origin. Today, look at every person you encounter and recognize them as your sibling, born of the same cosmic parents. More practically, use these verses as a diagnostic tool: When you feel light, clear, and healthy, recognize Sattva at work. But ask yourself, am I attached to this pleasant state? The goal is not to maximize Sattva but to recognize the witness who observes all three gunas without being bound by any. What would it feel like to appreciate happiness without grasping it?
